Prevention: Use certified crop and pasture seed to reduce the chance of contamination
Parthenium infested areas because they spread the seed
Parthenium seed introduction through water runoff from infested fields by soil bunding
Limit overgrazing to favour grasses to out compete
Monitoring: Annual erect broadleaved herb, 0.5-1.5 m high.
Leaves pale green and covered with short stiff hairs.
Rosette and lower stem leaves deeply divided and large; upper stem leaves are shorter and less divided.
White small compact flower heads (about 5 mm across) at the tips of branches
Regularly check edges of waterbodies, grazing places and vehicle tracks for rosettes; particulalry after rain
Regularly check fields for infestation and consider direct control whenever rosettes are present
Regular check for flowering and seed development to prevent seed set, spread and build up of seed bank in the field
Direct Control: Always wear long-sleeved clothes, gloves and, if possible, a mask to avoid contact with skin and respiratory tract as
Regularly uproot and bury any growing
Parthenium plants to limit establishment, making sure the entire root system is removed to prevent regrowth, to a depth of 6 inches
Avoid removal only by burning, mowing, slashing and ploughing as this may promote spread and regrowth
Maintain a regular weeding regime in pasture land to keep the pasture land free of the weed at all times
Restrictions: When using a pesticide, always wear protective clothing and follow the instructions on the product label, such as dosage
2,4-D (720g per litre of active ingredient per hectare) in low
Glyphosate (360g per litre of active ingredient per hecatre) in high
